title: Procedural Starfield World
weighting_note: SURF 65 covers point texture, distribution, contrast and editable shader controls. SCN 25 covers active World integration and the all-direction, infinite-distance environment behavior, following the benchmark World category. PIPE 10 covers delivery. No geometry or animation capability is added to this focused task.

rubric.criterion: The active World procedurally generates the rendered star signal.

scoring_rule.PASS: The entire starfield is generated by an editable procedural spatial pattern in the active World; no image/HDRI texture, star geometry, particle system, card, or finite dome supplies the stars, and the camera shows unobscured sky only.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: The active World shader procedurally contributes a visible star-like pattern. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: The active World shader does not procedurally contribute a visible star-like pattern.

verification.procedure: Trace the active World output to its source data, inspect all render-contributing scene elements and texture dependencies, then temporarily isolate World rendering to verify the visible star signal originates there.

rubric.criterion: Stars appear as fine rounded points with subtle falloff.

scoring_rule.PASS: Many stars have compact roughly circular cores, subtle edge falloff, and a fine scale with most only a few pixels wide in the 1920-by-1080 final image; large blobs, streaks, cell borders, and decorative starbursts are absent.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: The rendered starfield contains multiple localized bright point-like features. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: The rendered field lacks multiple localized bright point-like features.

verification.procedure: Render at the public delivery resolution and inspect full-frame and pixel-scale crops across several regions, assessing point extent, shape, and edge falloff.

rubric.criterion: The field has broadly even irregular coverage without obvious repeated structure.

scoring_rule.PASS: Stars cover the full view with broadly even density and natural local irregularity, without a square grid, obvious tiling, broad artificial bands, or concentration in one corner.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: Stars appear in multiple separated regions of the image. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: Stars do not appear in multiple separated image regions.

verification.procedure: Divide the same rendered view into spatial regions and compare qualitative coverage; inspect the whole frame for grid alignment, repeating patches, broad bands, and extreme density imbalance.

rubric.criterion: Neutral stars remain visible but faint against black or near-black space.

scoring_rule.PASS: The background between stars is black or near-black, with clearly distinguishable neutral-white points at full size and restrained overall brightness; gray wash, colored haze, and broad overexposure are absent.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: Visible stars are brighter than a predominantly dark background. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: Visible stars are not brighter than a predominantly dark background, or the star signal is absent.

verification.procedure: Inspect the actual-scene render at full size and sample representative star and inter-star pixels in a linear image output; assess neutral color, dark field, and restrained luminance against the finished reference.

rubric.criterion: The starfield covers all directions seamlessly and behaves as a stable distant environment.

scoring_rule.PASS: Upward, downward, and boundary-crossing views have comparable starfield character without seams, pole concentration, finite edges, or empty regions; camera translation at fixed orientation/lens and repeat renders preserve the directional pattern and point sizes.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: A starfield is visible in at least two different camera directions. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: A starfield is not visible in at least two different camera directions.

verification.procedure: Render six axis-oriented views plus a boundary-crossing pair at fixed exposure; translate a copy of the camera without rotating it or changing its lens, and compare repeated directional patterns and apparent star sizes.

rubric.criterion: Master brightness changes intensity without relocating stars.

scoring_rule.PASS: The master brightness control dims and brightens the same spatial pattern without relocating stars, and setting it to zero removes the star signal.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: An editable World control visibly changes star brightness. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: No editable World control visibly changes star brightness.

verification.procedure: On a copy, render baseline, reduced, increased, and zero master brightness values with fixed camera and exposure; compare star directions and signal intensities, then restore the baseline.

rubric.criterion: Pattern-scale and point-shaping controls effectively alter the procedural starfield.

scoring_rule.PASS: Pattern scale changes angular spacing and star frequency; a threshold or falloff control changes the size or prominence of bright regions while preserving black surroundings; both controls affect the active rendered World and the delivered values restore the restrained fine-point state.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: At least one editable pattern-scale or point-shaping control visibly changes the active World starfield. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: Neither an editable pattern-scale control nor a point-shaping control visibly changes the active World starfield.

verification.procedure: Vary pattern scale and point shaping separately in controlled renders with camera and brightness fixed; compare angular spacing/frequency and bright-region extent or prominence; verify connected influence on the active World and restore baseline values.

rubric.criterion: The editable World project, reproducible build, and authentic sky PNG are delivered.

scoring_rule.PASS: All three named files exist; the blend retains the requested active World and controls, build.py recreates them without external assets, and the 1920-by-1080 PNG is rendered from that scene using Blender 5.1.2 with Cycles GPU settings.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: A readable submission.blend contains the recognizable starfield World. Not all PASS conditions are met.
scoring_rule.FAIL: submission.blend is absent, unreadable, or lacks a recognizable starfield World.

verification.procedure: Open the blend and inspect the active World and rendering settings, run build.py in clean Blender 5.1.2, and compare the rebuilt World and a controlled render with the delivered blend and PNG. No runtime execution is claimed during authoring.
